name: Selin-6-en-4α-ol

papers.title: Chemical composition and biological activities of an essential oil from the aerial parts of Artemisia Gmelinii weber ex Stechm

research.basis: MeSH indexing and publication types of the most relevant PubMed records; counts are of papers in the sample, not findings.

vocabulary.structure: SEPIO assertion / evidence line / evidence item

evidence: Measured in 1 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.07% of total volatiles (0.014mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Selin-6-en-4α-ol is a sesquiterpene, a type of aromatic molecule found in the essential oils of fragrant plants. Molecules in this family typically contribute to the earthy, woody, or herbal aromas of the botanicals that produce them. A person is most likely to encounter it when smelling certain types of aromatic herbs.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in the essential oil of Artemisia gmelinii, a fragrant herb related to wormwood and mugwort.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to selin-6-en-4α-ol as part of their broader interest in the complex essential oils of Artemisia species. Early computational and laboratory work (Oxford level 5) is exploring how these plant extracts might interact with enzymes related to blood sugar regulation and cognitive health. If this bears out, it could help explain the traditional uses of these aromatic plants and highlight new natural compounds for metabolic and neurological support.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward this molecule being part of essential oils that may support cellular health against oxidative stress.
structure_function.basis: This rests on a single 2021 paper evaluating the chemical composition and biological activities of an Artemisia essential oil.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether selin-6-en-4α-ol actively contributes to the antioxidant capacity of Artemisia essential oils, which would mean it helps neutralize free radicals.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: An in vitro study isolating pure selin-6-en-4α-ol to measure its direct free-radical scavenging ability (such as a DPPH assay) compared to standard antioxidants.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Evidence is currently limited to a single laboratory study (Oxford level 5) looking at the broader essential oil that contains this molecule, with no direct clinical evidence available.
